office_does: Douglas County PUD's three elected commissioners set policy, budgets and electric rates for the county-wide utility that owns Wells Dam, for six-year terms.
race_blurb: Board president Molly Simpson, on the commission since 2015, defends the PUD's low rates and its 2024 rule that large new loads such as data centers buy their own market power. East Wenatchee Water District commissioner Nick Warner says the PUD is sitting on too much cash and should cut local bills instead of raising rates. All of Douglas County votes on the seat.

candidates.summary: Douglas County PUD commissioner since 2015 and current board president, a former Washington Apple Commission staffer running on low-cost Wells Dam power and making large new loads pay for growth.
highlights: Cites the 2024 policy requiring loads over 1.5 MW to buy power on the open market and pay a delivery fee: 'Growth needs to pay for growth' [S1]
Says Microsoft is the first customer on that plan and large crypto and data loads move to it by 2028 [S1]
Calls her approach fiscally conservative and says she is 'very protective' of Wells Dam [S1][S2]
Won the seat in 2014 with 58.7% and was re-elected unopposed in 2020 [S5][S6]

candidates.summary: East Wenatchee Water District commissioner, elected in 2017, running to stop rate increases he says only build PUD reserves, fund local discounts from out-of-area power sales, lower rates for schools and churches, and expand rural broadband.
highlights: Says PUD working capital grew from $60M to over $385M while 2025 rates rose 3% for residents and 8% for schools and churches [S2]
Would freeze rate increases meant to build reserves and offer 'Public Power Benefit' discounts [S2]
Proposes new transmission interconnections, wildfire mitigation, undergrounding and rural broadband [S2]
Elected water commissioner in 2017 and re-elected unopposed in 2023 [S3][S4]
